text: Solid work on knowledge distillation. The proposed method in Section 3.2 is well-described. My concern is with the teacher model selection — the authors use a 175B parameter model as teacher but don't discuss the cost. The student model in Table 3 achieves 95% of teacher performance, but the baseline (standard KD) achieves 94% — the improvement is marginal.

text: The paper presents a new approach to neural architecture search. The search space in Section 3 is well-defined. However, the search cost (Table 5) is 200 GPU-hours, which is not competitive with recent NAS methods that require <10 GPU-hours. The found architecture in Figure 4 looks similar to EfficientNet — is this a coincidence or expected?

text: Interesting paper on continual learning. The proposed method avoids catastrophic forgetting on the Split-CIFAR benchmark (Table 2). However, the method requires storing a replay buffer of 500 examples per task, which grows linearly with the number of tasks. This scalability issue is not discussed. The comparison with EWC in Table 3 uses different hyperparameters.

text: The paper proposes a new method for text summarization. The ROUGE scores in Table 1 are impressive. However, ROUGE is known to be a poor proxy for summary quality — the paper should include human evaluation. The proposed method generates summaries that are 30% longer than the reference (Table 3), which inflates ROUGE scores artificially.

text: Good paper on reinforcement learning from human feedback. The reward model in Section 3.1 is well-described. My concern is the evaluation: the authors use GPT-4 as the judge, but GPT-4 may be biased toward outputs that resemble its own style. The human evaluation in Table 4 uses only 3 annotators — this is insufficient for statistical significance.

text: Technically sound paper on point cloud processing. The proposed method in Section 3 is novel. However, the experiments in Section 5 only compare against SGD and Adam — the comparison should include more recent optimizers (AdamW, LAMB, Lion). text: Interesting work on self-supervised learning. The proposed pretext task in Section 3 is creative. text: Interesting work on federated learning. The proposed method reduces communication cost by 10x (Table 3). The experiments use IID data distribution, but federated learning is most relevant for non-IID settings.
